welcome:
Welcome to the Loki CLI Playground.
Query logs from a simulated production Loki instance.
Type 'help' for available commands, 'scenario' for guided labs.

steps.instruction: Start by discovering what log streams exist. List all available labels.
Good. Now see what values exist for the 'app' label.
Query the last hour of logs from the nginx reverse proxy.
Too many results. Filter for only HTTP 5xx errors in the nginx logs.
Now query the api service logs and filter for lines containing 'error' (case-insensitive).
Limit the output to the 5 most recent matching lines for a quick glance.
Check which label combinations (series) exist for app=api to understand its dimensions.
Finally, output the api error logs in JSON format for machine processing.
An alert fired: high error rate on the payments service. Start by checking the error rate over the last 5 minutes.
Count the total errors in the last 15 minutes to gauge severity.
Find the top 3 error sources to identify which pod is worst affected.
Read the actual error log lines from the payments service to understand the root cause.
The errors mention 'connection refused' to the database. Check the database logs for clues.
Correlate: check the nginx upstream errors to see if users were affected.
Use the Loki API directly to query the error rate over a time range for a dashboard check.
Confirm the database recovered by checking for recent 'ready to accept connections' messages.
steps.hint: Try: logcli query '{app="postgres"} |= "ready to accept connections"' --since=10m

commands.help:
Available commands:
  logcli query '<LogQL>'          — Run a log query and stream results
  logcli instant-query '<LogQL>'  — Run a metric query at a single point in time
  logcli labels [name]            — List labels or label values
  logcli series '<selector>'      — List series matching a selector
  curl <Loki API>                 — Query the Loki HTTP API directly

  Flags:
    --since=<duration>            — Lookback window (e.g. 1h, 30m, 7d)
    --limit=<N>                   — Max number of log lines to return
    --output=default|jsonl|raw    — Output format
    --forward                     — Show oldest entries first
    --no-labels                   — Suppress label output

  scenario                        — Start a guided lab
  clear                           — Clear the terminal
  help                            — Show this help
